stops.name: Dresden, the great hemorrhage and the failed cure
stops.campa: In August 1800 he begins to cough blood; the consumption that took Sophie and Erasmus has found him. After a severe hemorrhage in November he is carried to Dresden to be treated, but the cure does not hold. He is twenty-eight, director of the salt-works, betrothed, his novel unfinished, his fame just breaking. The Night he sang toward is coming for him in earnest now, no longer a vision on a hill but a fever in the lungs, drawing him down toward the beloved he never stopped following.

stops.name: Weissenfels, the death of Novalis, 25 March 1801
stops.campa: In January he asks to be brought home to his parents' house at Weissenfels. There he lies quiet and unafraid, the dying easy as a man going toward what he has long loved. On 25 March, his brother playing the clavier softly in the next room, he falls asleep and does not wake. Friedrich Schlegel is at the bedside. He is twenty-eight. He has kept faith with the Night: the singer who called death the bride goes to her at last, unresisting, the blue flower folding shut over him.
stops.quote: Hinüber wall' ich, / Und jede Pein / Wird einst ein Stachel / Der Wollust sein.
stops.quote_source: Novalis, Hymns to the Night, Fourth Hymn ('Over I journey, and every pain shall be a sting of delight')

stops.name: Alter Friedhof, Weissenfels: the grave, and the posthumous canon
stops.campa: He is buried in the Old Cemetery at Weissenfels, laid at last in the same earth of Saxony whose salts and strata he had governed. Within a year Tieck and Friedrich Schlegel gather his papers and give the world the Hymns to the Night, the Spiritual Songs, the unfinished Heinrich von Ofterdingen, the Novices of Sais. From the grave the fragments go out and multiply; the blue flower opens across a century of poets. The Night he sang keeps him, and answers every longing that will ever look up into it.
stops.quote: Zeit ist es, daß der Geist erwache... Nach oben geht der geheimnisvolle Weg.
stops.quote_source: Novalis, Fragments / Blüthenstaub ('Inward goes the mysterious way')
